vocabulary.meaning_en: information that makes people unhappy or worried
vocabulary.note_ar: news اسم غير معدود ويأخذ فعلًا مفردًا
vocabulary.note_en: News is uncountable and takes a singular verb.
vocabulary.example: I'm afraid I have some bad news.

vocabulary.meaning_en: tell people something unpleasant
vocabulary.example: A good manager delivers bad news clearly and kindly.

vocabulary.meaning_en: tell you the truth directly, without hiding anything
vocabulary.example: I've got to give it to you straight: we lost the contract.

vocabulary.meaning_en: what is likely to happen in the future
vocabulary.example: The outlook for next year is positive.

vocabulary.meaning_en: dark and without hope
vocabulary.example: The outlook is gloomy.

vocabulary.meaning_en: money a business earns after paying its costs
vocabulary.example: Our profits went up this year.

vocabulary.meaning_en: an official message that a company's profits will be lower than expected
vocabulary.example: The company had to announce a profit warning.

vocabulary.meaning_en: tell people something officially
vocabulary.example: The director will announce the results today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a time when a country's economy is weak
vocabulary.example: Many companies lost money during the recession.

vocabulary.meaning_en: one part of business or the economy
vocabulary.example: She works in the technology sector.

vocabulary.meaning_en: the people or area where you sell products
vocabulary.example: We plan to sell to the European market.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a plan to achieve a goal
vocabulary.example: Our new marketing strategy starts next month.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a manager who plans how to sell products
vocabulary.example: The marketing executive will join us next week.

vocabulary.meaning_en: losing your job because the company does not need it any more
vocabulary.example: There will be no redundancies this year.

vocabulary.meaning_en: without a job
vocabulary.example: He was unemployed for three months.

vocabulary.meaning_en: staying with and supporting a person or company
vocabulary.example: She has been a loyal employee for ten years.

vocabulary.meaning_en: at risk
vocabulary.example: Our jobs are on the line if sales don't improve.

vocabulary.meaning_en: become better
vocabulary.example: We need to improve our results.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in a formal way, by people in authority
vocabulary.example: The manager will officially welcome the team.

vocabulary.meaning_en: between different countries
vocabulary.example: Our phones can now make international calls.

fine_lines.title: profit vs benefit
fine_lines.explanation_ar: profit هو المال الذي تربحه الشركة، أما benefit فهو أي فائدة أو ميزة وليس بالضرورة مالًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Profit is money a business earns. A benefit is any advantage, not always money.

examples.sentence: The company made a profit of one million.
Free training is a benefit of this job.

fine_lines.title: outlook vs look
fine_lines.explanation_ar: outlook اسم بمعنى التوقعات للمستقبل، أما look فعل بمعنى ينظر أو يبدو.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Outlook is a noun: the likely future. Look is a verb: see or seem.

examples.sentence: The outlook for sales is good.

expressions.phrase: I've got to give it to you straight.
expressions.meaning_en: I must tell you the truth directly.
expressions.example: I've got to give it to you straight: sales are down.

expressions.meaning_en: The future does not look good.
expressions.example: After the bad results, the outlook is gloomy.

expressions.phrase: I've got to announce a profit warning.
expressions.meaning_ar: عليّ أن أعلن تحذيرًا من انخفاض الأرباح.
expressions.example: I'm sorry, everyone. I've got to announce a profit warning.
Things aren't looking good for our team this month.

expressions.phrase: You did a good job there. Well done.
expressions.example: Thanks for fixing the problem. You did a good job there.
Sales are falling. This calls for action.

expressions.phrase: I'm going to try my best.
expressions.meaning_en: I will work as hard as I can.
expressions.example: It's a new job, but I'm going to try my best.

grammar.title: have got to / have to for obligation
grammar.explanation_ar: I've got to = I have to: يجب عليّ (التزام). شائع في الكلام البريطاني غير الرسمي. بعده فعل مجرد.
grammar.explanation_en: I've got to = I have to: it is necessary. Common in spoken British English. Use the base verb after it.
examples: I've got to announce a profit warning.
We've got to improve our sales.
She's got to finish the report today.

grammar.title: Softening bad news
grammar.explanation_ar: لتلطيف الخبر السيئ نبدأ بعبارات مثل I'm afraid... أو I'm sorry to tell you... ثم نذكر الحقيقة بوضوح.
grammar.explanation_en: To make bad news softer, start with I'm afraid... or I'm sorry to tell you..., then say the facts clearly.
examples: I'm afraid the outlook is gloomy.
I'm sorry to tell you that we lost the order.
I'm afraid I have some bad news.

questions.question: "I've got to give it to you straight" means...
choices: I will tell you the truth directly
I will give you a present
questions.explanation_en: It means I will tell you the truth directly.

questions.question: "The outlook is gloomy" means...
choices: the future does not look good
questions.explanation_ar: outlook gloomy تعني أن المستقبل لا يبدو جيدًا.
questions.explanation_en: It means the future does not look good.

questions.question: A profit warning means profits will probably...
questions.explanation_ar: profit warning تحذير من انخفاض الأرباح.
questions.explanation_en: It warns that profits will go down.

questions.question: I've got ___ announce some bad news.
Money a business earns after costs is...
questions.explanation_en: Profit is the money earned after costs.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation_ar: news اسم غير معدود يأخذ فعلًا مفردًا is.
questions.explanation_en: News is uncountable: the news is.

questions.question: Which phrase softens bad news?
questions.explanation_en: I'm afraid makes bad news softer.

questions.question: "Your jobs are on the line" means your jobs are...
questions.explanation_ar: on the line تعني في خطر.
questions.explanation_en: On the line means at risk.

questions.question: A time when the economy is weak is a...
questions.explanation_en: A recession is a weak economy.

questions.question: The company wants to sell to the European ___.
questions.explanation_en: Market means the area where you sell.
